# Sizing lithium battery storage for rooftop photovoltaics

A rooftop array without storage curtails its midday surplus; a battery sized for
the evening peak recovers part of it. Read a year of interval data and find the
evening block the array cannot cover.

## Inverter coupling and backup loads

Coupled on the direct current side, the battery shares the inverter and the round
trip efficiency stays above ninety per cent. Coupled on the alternating current
side, it feeds the backup panel during an outage.

## Depth of discharge and cycle life

Depth of discharge is the fraction of nominal capacity the schedule uses, and it
sets the cycle life more than the chemistry alone.

A pack cycled to eighty per cent depth delivers roughly six thousand cycles
before the capacity falls to eighty per cent of nominal; the same pack limited to
sixty per cent depth reaches nearly ten thousand. Lithium iron phosphate
tolerates that deep cycling without the thermal margin nickel manganese cobalt
demands in a garage.

Sizing the pack to cover the whole evening trades capital cost against
replacement year, and the honest calculation uses the depth the schedule will
reach in the darkest week of winter, not the depth a summer day allows. A pack
sized for ninety per cent depth ages out in the fifth year of a ten year
payback, which is the number the sales sheet never prints.

Reserve capacity for a winter week pushes the pack up one size bracket and pays
for itself in a single outage, which is why the schedule and the reserve should
be sized together.
